stem: A nursing student asks why an arterial blood gas is preferred over a venous blood gas when direct assessment of arterial oxygenation is required. Which explanation is best?

options.A: PaO2 is measured from arterial blood to assess oxygenation, and arterial-venous differences are especially large for oxygen partial pressure.
options.B: Arterial sampling is mainly a research method because arterial oxygen measurements add little clinically useful information beyond venous gases.
options.C: Venous PO2 can be substituted directly for arterial PaO2 because oxygen partial pressure differs minimally between arterial and venous blood.
options.D: Arterial sampling is preferred primarily to measure glucose, while oxygenation and blood-gas values are more accurately obtained from venous blood.

rationale: The July 2026 StatPearls/NCBI update states that ABG analysis measures PaO2 and PaCO2 and that PaO2 provides information about oxygenation. It specifically identifies PaO2 measurement as a primary reason for obtaining an arterial specimen because arterial-venous differences are most pronounced for PO2; venous PO2 is typically substantially lower. Therefore A is correct. B and D misstate the clinical purpose of arterial sampling, and C incorrectly treats venous PO2 as interchangeable with arterial PaO2.
educational_objective: Explain why arterial rather than venous sampling is required when direct PaO2-based assessment of arterial oxygenation is needed.
source_organization: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI Bookshelf) / StatPearls
source_document_title: Arterial Blood Gas Analysis: Fundamentals, Interpretation, and Clinical Utility
source_version_date: StatPearls 2026 edition; last update July 5, 2026; live NCBI page retrieved 2026-08-26
source_locator: Introduction: ABG measures PaO2 and PaCO2; PaO2 provides oxygenation information. Specimen Requirements and Procedure: PaO2 measurement is the primary reason for an arterial specimen because arterial-venous differences are most pronounced for PO2; venous PO2 is typically ~60 mm Hg lower.
source_claim_supported: Arterial PaO2 directly assesses oxygenation and differs substantially from venous PO2, so venous PO2 is not interchangeable for direct arterial oxygenation assessment.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — interpret diagnostic tests and laboratory findings.
correction_summary: Balanced option lengths and preserved the direct PaO2-specific reason for arterial rather than venous sampling.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — the July 2026 NCBI source explicitly identifies PaO2 as a primary reason for arterial sampling and documents a large arterial-venous PO2 difference.
